en: The Sutra on the Original Vows of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, Volume One.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the Tang Dynasty.
Chapter One: The Chapter on Supernatural Powers in the Palace of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven. Chapter One: The Chapter on Supernatural Powers in the Palace of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, preaching the Dharma for his mother.
At that time, unspeakably unspeakable numbers of all Buddhas and great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas from immeasurable worlds throughout the ten directions all came to assemble there.

They praised Śākyamuni Buddha, who, within this world of five turbidities, manifests the power of inconceivable great wisdom and supernatural penetrations to subdue beings of stubborn and violent nature, and who understands the dharmas of suffering and pleasure; each dispatched an attendant to inquire after the World-Honored One’s well-being.

At that time, the Tathāgata smiled and emitted hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of great clouds of light—namely, the great cloud of perfect light, the great cloud of compassionate light, the great cloud of wisdom light, the great cloud of prajñā light, the great cloud of samādhi light, the great cloud of auspiciousness light, the great cloud of merit light, the great cloud of virtue light, the great cloud of refuge light, and the great cloud of praise light.

Having emitted such unspeakable clouds of light as these, there further issued forth various subtle and wondrous sounds—namely, the sound of the *dāna-pāramitā*, the sound of the *śīla-pāramitā*, the sound of the *kṣānti-pāramitā*, the sound of the *vīrya-pāramitā*, the sound of the *dhyāna-pāramitā*, the sound of the *prajñā-pāramitā*; the sound of compassion, the sound of sympathetic joy and equanimity, the sound of liberation, the sound of the untainted (*anāsrava*), the sound of wisdom, the sound of great wisdom, the sound of the lion’s roar, the sound of the great lion’s roar, the sound of the thundering clouds, and the sound of the great thundering clouds.

After these unspeakably unspeakable sounds had been uttered, immeasurable billions of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas from the Sahā world and other lands also gathered at the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven palace.

The so-called gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven; the Brahmakāyika Heaven, the Brahmapurohita Heaven, the Mahābrahma Heaven; the Parīttābha Heaven, the Apramāṇābha Heaven, the Ābhāsvara Heaven; the Parīttaśubha Heaven, the Apramāṇaśubha Heaven, the Śubhakṛtsna Heaven; the Puṇyaprasava Heaven, the Bṛhatphala Heaven, the Avṛha Heaven, the Atapa Heaven, the Sudṛśa Heaven, the Sudarśana Heaven, and the Akaniṣṭha Heaven; up to the gods of the Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-perception—all these hosts of devas, nāgas, spirits, and so forth, assembled together.

Furthermore, there were deities from other lands, as well as the ocean deities, river deities, stream deities, tree deities, mountain deities, earth deities, marsh deities, crop deities, day deities, night deities, space deities, celestial deities, food-and-drink deities, and plant deities of the Sahā world; all such deities gathered together for this assembly.

Furthermore, there were great ghost kings from other lands as well as from the Sahā world—namely, the Ghost King of Evil Eyes, the Ghost King Who Devours Blood, the Ghost King Who Devours Vital Essence, the Ghost King Who Devours Fetuses and Eggs, the Ghost King Who Spreads Disease, the Ghost King Who Governs Poisons, the Ghost King of Compassionate Heart, the Ghost King of Benefit and Fortune, and the Ghost King of Great Affection and Respect—all such ghost kings came to assemble.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta:

“Observe all these Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as the devas, nāgas, ghosts, and spirits—from this world and other worlds, from this land and other lands—who have now gathered and arrived at the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven; do you know their number?”
Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Even if one were to employ my supernormal powers to investigate for a thousand kalpas, it could not be known.”
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī:
“Even though I observe with my Buddha-eye, I cannot exhaustively enumerate them.

All of these are those whom the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, since the distant kalpas of the past, has already delivered, shall deliver, or has yet to deliver; those he has already brought to fulfillment, shall bring to fulfillment, or has yet to bring to fulfillment.”
Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I have long cultivated roots of goodness in the past and have realized unimpeded wisdom; having heard what the Buddha has said, I shall immediately accept it with faith.”

The śrāvakas of the lesser fruit, the eight classes of devas and nāgas, and all sentient beings of future ages, though they hear the Tathāgata’s words of truth, will certainly harbor doubts; even if they receive them upon the crown of their heads, they will not avoid giving rise to slander.

We only pray that the World-Honored One will explain in detail what practices the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha performed and what vows he established while on the stage of a causal bodhisattva, by which he was able to accomplish such inconceivable deeds.
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī:

"Suppose, for example, that all the grasses, trees, forests, rice, hemp, bamboo, reeds, mountains, rocks, and motes of dust within a trichiliocosm were each counted as one Ganges River; and each Ganges River were counted as one grain of sand; and each grain of sand were counted as one world-system."
Within a single world-system, there is one dust mote for every eon; within each eon, the number of dust motes accumulated could all be counted as eons.
Since the time the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha realized the fruit of the tenth stage, the number of eons has been a thousand times greater than the aforementioned analogy.
How much more so for Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, who dwells in the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas! Mañjuśrī,
the majestic power and vows of this bodhisattva are inconceivable.

If, in future ages, there are good men or good women who hear the name of this Bodhisattva, or praise him, or gaze upon and worship him, or recite his name, or make offerings to him—even by painting, carving, or modeling his image with lacquer—such persons shall be reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven a hundred times and never fall into the evil realms.
“Mañjuśrī! This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, in the distant past, incalculably and inexpressibly many eons ago, was the son of a great elder.”
At that time, there was a Buddha in the world named Siṃhavikrāntagāmin-saṃpanna-sarvacaryā Tathāgata.
When the son of the elder saw the Buddha’s marks and signs, adorned by a thousand merits, he asked that Buddha:
"By performing what practices and making what vows did you obtain these marks?"
Then the Tathāgata Siṃhavikrīḍita, who was fully endowed with the ten thousand practices, told the son of the elder:
"If you wish to realize this body, you must for a long time deliver all sentient beings who are suffering."
“Mañjuśrī! At that time, the son of the elder made this vow, saying:

‘From now until the end of the future, throughout incalculable kalpas, I shall extensively employ skillful means for the sake of these sentient beings of the six realms who suffer from their transgressions, so as to bring them all to liberation; only then will I myself attain the Buddha-way.’”
"Because he established this great vow before that Buddha, he has remained a bodhisattva even until now, for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of unspeakable eons."
"Furthermore, in the past, during inconceivable incalculable kalpas ago, there was a Buddha in that world named Buddha-Flower Samādhi-Sovereign King Tathāgata."
The lifespan of that Buddha was four hundred thousand million *koṭi* *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas.
During the period of the Semblance Dharma, there was a Brahmin girl whose past merit was profound and vast, whom all held in high esteem;
whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, she was protected by the devas.
Her mother believed in heterodox teachings and constantly disparaged the Triple Gem.
At that time, the noble woman extensively explained skillful means to exhort and guide her mother, causing her to give rise to right view.
However, the mother of this girl had not yet attained full faith; before long, her life ended and her spirit fell into the Avīci Hell.

At that time, the Brahmin girl knew that while her mother was alive she had not believed in cause and effect, and calculated that she must follow her karma and would certainly be reborn in an evil realm.
He then sold his house and estate to extensively seek out incense, flowers, and various ritual implements, making grand offerings at the stūpas and temples of former Buddhas.

He beheld the Tathāgata King of the Samādhi of Enlightenment-Flower Sovereignty; his image was within a temple, modeled and painted with a majestic countenance, perfectly complete in its dignified and solemn appearance.
At that time, the Brahmin woman gazed upon the Honored One’s countenance and felt a redoubled sense of reverence and admiration.
She thought to herself:

"The Buddha is named the Greatly Awakened One and possesses all-encompassing wisdom. If he were still in the world when my mother passed away, had I come to question him, he would surely have known her whereabouts."
At that time, the Brahmin woman wept for a long while, gazing longingly after the Tathāgata.
Suddenly, she heard a voice from the air saying:
"O weeping noble lady!
"Do not fall into sorrow; I shall now show you the place where your mother has gone.
The Brahmin girl joined her palms toward the sky and addressed the void, saying:
"What divine power is this that relieves my anxiety?"
"Since I lost my mother, I have remembered her with longing day and night, yet there is no one from whom I may inquire about the realm in which she was reborn.
At that time, a voice resounded from the sky, addressing the girl once more:
"I am the one whom you have gazed upon and paid homage to; I am the Tathāgata Padmavṛṣabhavikrāmin-guṇarāja of the past."
"Seeing that you remember your mother with a devotion far exceeding the common lot of sentient beings, I have come to inform you.
Upon hearing these words, the Brahmin girl threw herself to the ground, her limbs and joints all bruised and broken.
Supported on both sides by his attendants, he regained consciousness after a long while and addressed Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"I pray that the Buddha, out of compassion, will quickly tell me the realm where my mother has been reborn.
My body and mind are now such that death will come before long."
At that time, the Tathāgata King of the Samādhi of the Sovereignty of Awakening Flowers said to the noble daughter:
"Once you have finished making offerings, simply return home early.
Sit upright and contemplate my name, and you shall immediately know the place where your mother has been reborn."
Then the Brahmin woman, having prostrated before the Buddha, immediately returned to her home.
Because she was mindful of her mother, she sat upright for one day and one night, recollecting the Tathāgata King of Sovereignty over the Awakening Flower Samādhi.
Suddenly he saw himself arrive at the shore of a sea.
Its waters were surging and boiling; there were many malevolent beasts, all with bodies of iron, flying and running upon the sea, galloping back and forth in pursuit of one another.
He saw hundreds of thousands of men and women appearing and disappearing within the sea, being seized and devoured by various evil beasts.

He also saw yakṣas of diverse forms—some with many hands, many eyes, many feet, and many heads; their mouths and fangs protruded, and their sharp teeth were like swords. These beings drove the sinners toward the evil beasts, while they themselves clawed and tore at them, bringing their heads and feet together.
Their forms were of ten thousand kinds, and one did not dare look at them for long.
At that time, because of the power of her mindfulness of the Buddha, the Brahmin woman was naturally free from fear.
A king of ghosts named Wudu (Non-Venomous) bowed his head in greeting and came forward to meet her, saying to the Holy Woman:
"Excellent! For what reason has the Bodhisattva come here?
At that time, the Brahmin girl asked the King of Ghosts.
"What place is this? Wudu replied,
"This is the first layer of the ocean on the western side of the Great Iron Ring Mountains."
The noble lady asked:
"I have heard that within the Iron Ring Mountains (Cakravāḍa), the hells are situated in their midst;
is this true? Avyāpāda replied:
"There truly is hell.
The noble lady asked,
"How may I now reach the place of that hell?"
The Woman Without Poison replied, "If it is not through spiritual power, then it must be through karmic force; without these two things, one can never arrive.
The Holy Woman asked again:
"For what reason does this water surge and boil?
Why are there so many sinful people and wicked beasts here? Wudu replied:

"These are sentient beings from Jambudvīpa who have recently died after committing evil deeds; forty-nine days having passed, no one has succeeded them to perform meritorious acts for their rescue from suffering and hardship. Since they possessed no roots of goodness during life, they must now proceed naturally across this sea toward the hells, as dictated by the retribution of their original karma."
Ten thousand yojanas to the east of this sea, there is another sea whose suffering is twice as great as this one.
To the east of that sea, there is yet another sea whose suffering is again doubled.
"Summoned by the evil causes of the three karmas, this place is what is collectively called the Ocean of Karma.
The Holy Woman then asked the King of Ghosts, Wudu:
"Where is hell located?"
Wu Du replied: "Within the three seas lie great hells numbering in the hundreds of thousands, each distinct from the others.
As for the major ones, there are eighteen."
"Next there are five hundred, suffering immeasurable poison.
Next there are a thousand, likewise suffering immeasurable pain.
The Holy Woman again asked the Great King of Ghosts:
"My mother has been dead for no long time; I do not know to which realm her spirit has gone.
The King of Ghosts asked the Holy Woman, "In what practices did the Mother of the Bodhisattva engage during her life?"
The noble woman replied:
"My mother holds wrong views and reviles the Triple Gem.
Even if she should momentarily believe, she immediately becomes disrespectful again."
"Although his death was but recent, we do not yet know the place where he has been reborn. Wudu asked,
"What are the family name and given name of the Bodhisattva’s mother?"
The noble lady replied:
"Both my father and my mother are of the Brahmin caste.
My father’s name is Śīlasuprabha, and my mother’s name is Mṛgajā."
Vītamala joined his palms and addressed the Bodhisattva, saying:
"I pray that the Noble One will return to your original dwelling and not harbor sorrow, longing, or attachment.
It has now been three days since the sinful woman Śyāmāvatī was born in heaven."
"It is said that because a filial son has made offerings and cultivated merit for his mother by giving to the stūpa and monastery of the Tathāgata Awakening Flower Samādhi Sovereign King,

not only has the mother of the Bodhisattva been liberated from hell, but even those who committed the crimes of the Avīci Hell have all attained happiness this very day and have been reborn together."
When the king of ghosts had finished speaking, he joined his palms and withdrew.
The Brahmin girl then returned as if from a dream.
Having awakened to this matter, she stood before the stupa and image of the Tathāgata King of Samādhi Sovereign of Awakening Flowers and made a great vow:

“I vow that throughout all future kalpas, for all sentient beings who ought to undergo the suffering of retribution for their transgressions, I shall extensively employ skillful means to bring them to liberation.
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī: “The ghost-king named ‘Poisonless’ at that time was none other than the present-day Bodhisattva Vasumitra.”
"The Brahmin woman was none other than Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.

**Chapter Two: The Assembly of Manifested Bodies** At that time, from hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of inconceivable, unfathomable, immeasurable, ineffable, and infinite asaṃkhyeya worlds, all the manifested bodies of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattvas from every location within the hells gathered together in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven Palace.

By the supernatural power of the Tathāgata, from each direction there arrived those who had attained liberation and emerged from the path of karma—also numbering in the hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas—who together held fragrant flowers to make offerings to the Buddha.
All those who came together with him were, through the transformative teaching of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, rendered forever irreversible from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
These multitudes have, for kalpas long past, wandered through birth and death, suffering in the six realms without a moment's rest.
Because of the vast compassion and profound vows of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, each has attained the realization of the fruit.
Having arrived in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, his heart was filled with exultation; he gazed up at the Tathāgata, his eyes never for a moment averting.

At that time, the World-Honored One extended his golden-hued arm and rubbed the crowns of the heads of the countless, inconceivable, immeasurable, ineffable, and infinite *asaṃkhyeya* world-systems of the various emanations of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, saying:

"In this world of five turbidities, I have taught and transformed such stubborn and unruly sentient beings, causing their minds to be subdued and leading them to abandon the heterodox and return to the orthodox."
Even among those who have reached the eleventh or twelfth stage, the habituation to evil still persists.
I, too, shall manifest a thousand, ten thousand, and even a hundred million bodies, extensively establishing skillful means.
There may be those with sharp faculties who, upon hearing this, will immediately believe and accept it.
Some possess the fruits of goodness, which they diligently encourage others to achieve;
some are dull-witted, returning only after long transformation;
and some have heavy karma, failing to give rise to reverence.
For such classes of sentient beings, each distinct in their differences, he manifests divided bodies to deliver them.

He may manifest in the body of a man, or the body of a woman; he may manifest in the body of a deva or a nāga, or the body of a spirit or a ghost; or he may manifest as mountains, forests, rivers, plains, ponds, pools, springs, and wells—benefiting humanity and delivering them all.

Sometimes manifesting in the body of Śakra, the Lord of Devas; sometimes manifesting in the body of Brahmā, the King of the Brahma-world; sometimes manifesting in the body of a Cakravartin King; sometimes manifesting in the body of a householder; sometimes manifesting in the body of a king; sometimes manifesting in the body of a minister; sometimes manifesting in the body of a subordinate official; sometimes manifesting in the bodies of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās; and even manifesting in the bodies of śrāvakas, arhats, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas, thereby bringing them to transformation and deliverance.
"It is not only my body that appears before you alone.
Observe how, through many kalpas of diligent toil, I have delivered such beings as these—those who are difficult to transform, stubborn, and burdened by the suffering of their transgressions."
As for those who have not yet been tamed, they will follow the retribution of their karma.
If they fall into the evil realms and undergo great suffering, you should then remember my earnest entrustment to you while I was in the palace of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.

May all sentient beings in the Sahā world, from now until the appearance of Maitreya in this world, be brought to complete liberation, forever freed from all suffering, and encounter a Buddha who grants them the prophecy of enlightenment.
At that time, the various manifestations of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva from all worlds reunited into a single form; weeping with sorrowful longing, he addressed his Buddha, saying:
"Since the distant kalpas of the past, I have been guided by the Buddha, enabling me to obtain inconceivable spiritual powers and to possess great wisdom."
My manifested bodies fill worlds as numerous as the sands of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Ganges Rivers.
In each world, I manifest hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodies.

Each body delivers hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of people, causing them to take refuge in and revere the Triple Gem, forever leave behind birth and death, and attain the bliss of Nirvana.

However, regarding whatever wholesome deeds they perform within the Buddha-dharma—be it a single hair, a single drop, a single grain of sand, a single speck of dust, or even something as slight as a hair’s breadth—I shall gradually deliver them and cause them to attain great benefit.
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will not worry about sentient beings of future generations who commit evil deeds.
Thus he addressed the Buddha three times, saying:
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will not worry about sentient beings of future generations who commit evil deeds."
At that time, the Buddha praised Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
"I join you in your joy.
You have been able to fulfill the great vows you made throughout kalpas past; now that your extensive work of saving beings is nearly complete, you shall immediately realize Bodhi.
Chapter Three: Observing the Karmic Conditions of Sentient Beings At that time, the Buddha’s mother, Lady Māyā, joined her palms in reverence and asked Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva:
“Noble One! Among the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa, there are differences in the karma they create; what are the specific matters regarding the retributions they receive?
Kṣitigarbha replied:

"In worlds numbering in the millions, as well as their respective lands, some may have hells and some may not; some may have women and some may not; some may have the Buddha-dharma and some may not—and even regarding śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, it is likewise so."
"It is not only in the hells that the retribution for offenses is of one kind.
Māyādevī addressed the Bodhisattva again:
"I would further wish to hear about the retributions for offenses in Jambudvīpa and the evil destinies they induce."
Kṣitigarbha replied:
"O Holy Mother!
I pray that you will listen and accept my brief explanation."
The Mother of Buddhas replied,
"I pray that the Noble One will speak.
At that time, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva addressed the Holy Mother, saying:
"Regarding the retributions for sins in Jambudvīpa, the names [of the hells] are as follows:

if there are sentient beings who are unfilial toward their parents, or even go so far as to kill them, they shall fall into the Avīci Hell, remaining there for thousands of myriads of koṭis of kalpas with no prospect of escape."

If there are sentient beings who shed the blood of a Buddha, slander the Triple Gem, or show no reverence for the honored scriptures, they shall likewise fall into the Avīci Hell, where for thousands of myriads of koṭis of kalpas they will have no hope of escape.

If there are sentient beings who plunder or damage the permanent property of the Sangha, defile the monks or nuns, or indulge in sexual misconduct within a monastery, or commit murder or injury—such as these shall fall into the Avīci Hell, where for thousands of millions of billions of kalpas they will have no hope of escape.

If there are sentient beings who falsely assume the guise of śramaṇas while their minds are not those of śramaṇas; who misappropriate and consume the permanent endowments of the Sangha; who deceive laypeople and violate the precepts; and who commit various kinds of evil—such as these shall fall into the Avīci Hell for thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, with no hope of escape.

If there are sentient beings who steal or pilfer the permanent property of the Sangha—be it grain, rice, food, drink, clothing, or even a single item taken without it being given—they shall fall into the Avīci Hell, where they will remain for thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, with no prospect of escape.
Kṣitigarbha replied: "O Holy Mother!
If there are sentient beings who commit such sins that they ought to fall into the five Avīci hells, they shall not obtain even a single moment's respite from suffering."
Lady Māyā addressed Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva once more, saying:
"What is meant by the 'Avīci Hell'? Kṣitigarbha replied:
"Holy Mother!
All the hells are within the Great Iron Ring Mountains.
Of these great hells, there are eighteen locations."
Next there are five hundred, each with a distinct name;
next there are one thousand, their names likewise distinct.

As for the Avīci Hell, its city walls encircle more than eighty thousand *li*; the city is made entirely of iron, rising ten thousand *li* high, with masses of fire atop the walls, leaving little room for gaps.
Within that city of hells, various prisons are interconnected, each with its own distinct name.
There is, however, one prison alone named Avīci (the Uninterrupted).

This hell is eighteen thousand li in circumference; its walls are one thousand li high and are made entirely of iron. The fire from above penetrates to the bottom, and the fire from below reaches to the top. Iron snakes and iron dogs, vomiting flames, run and chase one another, galloping back and forth atop the prison walls.
In the prison there is a bed that extends for ten thousand *li*.
When one person undergoes punishment, he sees his own body lying and filling the entire bed.
When ten million people undergo punishment, each likewise sees their own body filling the bed.
Induced by their various karmas, they receive such retributions.
Furthermore, all these sinners undergo every kind of suffering.
Thousands and hundreds of yakṣas and malevolent spirits, with mouths and fangs like swords and eyes like flashes of lightning, and hands with copper-clawed nails, drag and pull the sinners along.

Furthermore, there are yakṣas who grasp great iron spears and strike the bodies of the offenders; they may strike their mouths and noses, or their bellies and backs, tossing them into the air to catch them as they fall, or placing them upon beds.
Furthermore, there are iron hawks that devour the eyes of the sinners;
there are iron snakes that coil around their necks.

Long nails are driven into all their joints; their tongues are pulled out and plowed over; their entrails are extracted and hacked to pieces; molten copper is poured into their mouths, and glowing iron is wrapped around their bodies.
Undergoing ten thousand deaths and a thousand births, such is the retribution of karma;
it may last for billions of kalpas, with no foreseeable end to seeking escape.
When this world-system perishes, one takes temporary residence in another realm.
When this world-system is next destroyed, beings migrate to other regions;
when those regions are destroyed, they successively migrate to one another.
Once this world-system has been reformed, they return once again.
Such is the retribution for the offense of immediate retribution (*ānantarya*).
Furthermore, it is called "immediate" because it is brought about by five types of actions. What are these five?
First, one undergoes retribution day and night for kalpas on end without any interval; therefore, it is called "Avīci" (Without Interval).
Second, whether there is only one person or many people, the retribution is fully realized; therefore, it is called "Avīci."

Third, there are the instruments of punishment: the pitchfork and the staff; hawks, snakes, wolves, and dogs; the pestle and the millstone; the saw and the chisel; the meat-chopper and the boiling cauldron; the iron net and the iron rope; the iron donkeys and iron horses; raw leather bound around the head; molten iron poured over the body; swallowing iron pellets when hungry; and drinking molten iron when thirsty.
From the end of one eon to the next, for *nayuta* of years, the torments continue in succession without any interruption; therefore, it is called "Uninterrupted" (*Avīci*).

Fourth, regardless of whether one is male or female, Qiang, Hu, Yi, or Di, old or young, noble or lowly, or whether one is a dragon, a spirit, a deva, or a ghost—due to the karmic retribution of their sinful deeds, all undergo these sufferings equally; therefore, it is called "Uninterrupted."

Fifth, if one falls into this hell, from the moment of entry until the passing of hundreds of thousands of kalpas, one undergoes ten thousand deaths and ten thousand births every single day and night.
One cannot find even a single moment’s respite to remain still.
"Only when their karma is exhausted can they receive rebirth.
Because they are thus continuously linked, it is called 'uninterrupted'.
Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha addressed the Holy Mother, saying:
"Such is a rough description of the Avīci Hell.

If one were to explain in detail the names of the various hells, such as the Vaitaraṇī River, and the manifold sufferings therein, one would not reach the end of the account even in the course of an entire kalpa."
Upon hearing this, Lady Māyā was filled with sorrow; she joined her palms, prostrated herself, and withdrew.
Chapter Four: The Sentient Beings of Jambudvīpa and Their Karmic Repercussions At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”

Relying on the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha-Tathāgata, I pervade hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of worlds, dividing this physical body to rescue and deliver all sentient beings who are subject to karmic retribution.
Were it not for the power of the Tathāgata’s great compassion, such transformations could not have been performed.
Now, having further received the Buddha’s entrustment, until the time when Ajita attains Buddhahood, I am sent to deliver and liberate the sentient beings within the six realms of existence.
"So be it, World-Honored One; please do not have such concerns.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva:
"All sentient beings who have not yet attained liberation possess natures and consciousnesses that are not fixed."
Evil habits form karmic bonds, while good habits yield fruits; whether acting for good or evil, one is driven by external conditions.

These are all one's parents, sons, daughters, younger brothers, younger sisters, spouses, and kinsmen from one lifetime, ten lifetimes, a hundred lifetimes, or a thousand lifetimes past; they are currently in the evil realms, unable to escape, and have no place to hope for rescue through the power of merit. Puguang! By means of your supernatural power, dispatch these attendants so that they may, before the images of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, read this sutra with a sincere mind, either reading it themselves or requesting someone else to read it.
This shall be recited three times, or seven times.
When these evil associates of the miserable realms have heard the sound of this scripture for the prescribed number of recitations, they shall attain liberation;
even within their dreams, they shall never see them again.
"Furthermore, Puguang!

If in future ages there are those of low station, whether slaves or servants, or even those who are not free, who become aware of their past karma and wish to repent, they should with a sincere heart gaze upon and pay homage to the image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. For as little as seven days, they should recite the Bodhisattva’s name ten thousand times."

"Such persons as these, after the exhaustion of this retribution, will for ten million lifetimes always be born into noble and honorable circumstances, never again undergoing the sufferings of the three evil realms. Furthermore, Puguang!

If, in a future age, within Jambudvīpa, there are among the kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, elders, householders, and all other people, as well as those of various castes and lineages, who have given birth to a child—whether male or female—within seven days one should promptly recite this inconceivable sūtra for them, and furthermore, chant the name of the Bodhisattva ten thousand times.
This newborn child, whether male or female, having previously possessed karmic retribution, now attains liberation; they become peaceful, easy to nourish, and their lifespan increases.
If one receives such merit and gives rise to it, their peace and happiness, as well as their lifespan, will further increase. Furthermore, Puguang!

If sentient beings in future ages, on the first, eighth, fourteenth, fifteenth, eighteenth, twenty-third, twenty-fourth, twenty-eighth, twenty-ninth, or even the thirtieth day of the month—on these various days, all karmic offenses are gathered together and their lightness or gravity is determined.

Among the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa in the south, every movement of body and every stirring of thought is without exception karma and without exception sin; how much more so for those who indulge their passions in killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and lying—these hundreds and thousands of transgressions?

If one can, on these ten days of fasting, recite this sutra once before images of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and various worthy sages, then within a hundred *yojanas* to the east, west, south, and north, there shall be no calamities or disasters.
While residing in this household, whether they be elders or juniors, for hundreds of thousands of years in the present and the future, they shall forever be free from the evil realms.

If one can recite this once on each of the ten days of fasting, it will ensure that in this present life, no sudden illnesses shall afflict those in the household, and their food and clothing shall be abundant.

"Therefore, Puguang! You should know that the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha possesses such unspeakable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of acts of great majestic power for the benefit of others."
The sentient beings of Jambudvīpa have a great karmic affinity with this Great Being.

Should these beings hear the Bodhisattva’s name, see his image, or even hear three characters, five words, a single verse, or a single line of this sutra, they will experience extraordinary, wondrous peace and happiness in the present life; and in future worlds, throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of births, they shall always be handsome and well-proportioned, and be born into noble and honorable families.

At that time, after the Bodhisattva Puguang had heard the Buddha-Tathāgata praise and extol the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, he knelt on his right knee with palms joined and addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"I have long known that this Great Being possesses such inconceivable supernormal powers as well as the power of his great vow.
For the sake of future sentient beings, so that they may know of these benefits, I have questioned the Tathāgata; indeed, I receive this with my head bowed."
"Bhagavān! What should this sutra be named?
How should I propagate it?"
The Buddha told Puguang:
"This sutra has three names:
the first is 'The Original Vow of Kṣitigarbha,' it is also called 'The Original Conduct of Kṣitigarbha,' and it is also called 'The Sutra on the Power of Kṣitigarbha’s Original Vow.'"
Because this Bodhisattva, throughout kalpas long ago, made great and profound vows to benefit sentient beings, you all should propagate [this teaching] in accordance with those vows.
Having heard this, Puguang joined his palms in reverence, paid obeisance, and withdrew.

Chapter Seven: Benefits for the Living and the Deceased.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
When I observe the sentient beings of this Jambudvīpa, every movement of thought and stirring of mind is nothing but transgression.
Even when they happen to obtain wholesome benefits, they mostly retreat from their initial resolve.”
If they encounter adverse conditions, these states increase with every thought-moment.
Such people are like those treading through mud while carrying heavy stones; as they grow increasingly exhausted and the burden heavier, their footprints sink deeper.

If one encounters a spiritual friend who relieves or even entirely removes one's burden, it is because that spiritual friend possesses great power; furthermore, they provide mutual assistance and encourage one to stand firm on one's feet. Once one has reached level ground, one must avoid the evil paths so as not to experience them again.
“World-Honored One!
When sentient beings habituate themselves to evil, it begins from the slightest degree and soon reaches the measureless.
For all such beings who possess these habits, when they approach the end of their lives, their parents and kinsmen should establish merit on their behalf to provide for their journey ahead.”
Or they may suspend banners and canopies and light oil lamps; or they may recite and chant the honored sutras; or they may make offerings to images of the Buddha and various holy beings.

Even down to chanting the names of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Pratyekabuddhas—each name and each title—so that they pass through the ear-faculty of the person at the point of death, or are heard within their fundamental consciousness (*ālayavijñāna*).

Regarding the evil karma created by these sentient beings, if one calculates the resulting retribution, they would certainly fall into the evil realms; however, because their relatives cultivate this sacred cause for them at the time of death, all such transgressions are entirely extinguished.

If, after their death, one can further perform extensive meritorious deeds within the seven weeks following their passing, one can cause these sentient beings to forever leave the evil realms and be reborn among humans or devas to enjoy supreme and wondrous bliss; thus, their current kinsmen will receive immeasurable benefit.
"Therefore, I now, before the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and the assembly of devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, humans, and non-humans, exhort the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa:

on the day of their final passing, they must be careful not to commit acts of killing or create other evil conditions—such as sacrificing to ghosts and spirits or seeking aid from various malevolent demons."

Why is this? All such acts as killing and even performing sacrifices do not provide the slightest benefit to the deceased; they merely create conditions for karmic retribution, causing their gravity to increase further and further.

Even if, in a future life or in the present birth, one attains the factors of holiness and is reborn among humans or devas, should they, at the point of death, be surrounded by kinsmen who create such evil causes, this will cause the deceased to face the retribution of their transgressions; yet, it may also lead them to be born later in a favorable realm.

How much more so for one who is at the point of death, having never cultivated even a small root of goodness during their lifetime; as each person must undergo the evil realms according to their own fundamental karma, how can one bear to have their kinsmen further increase that karma?
It is like a person who has come from a distant land, having gone without food for three days and carrying a burden of more than a hundred pounds.
Suddenly encountering a neighbor, they further add a small amount of goods; because of this, they become even more exhausted and weighed down.
“World-Honored One!

When I observe the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa, I see that within the teachings of all Buddhas, even regarding virtuous deeds as small as a single hair, a single drop, a single grain of sand, or a single speck of dust—such benefits as these are entirely attained by them on their own.”

When these words were spoken, there was in the assembly an elder named Mahāpratibhāna—this elder had long since realized the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) and, having brought beings to liberation throughout the ten directions, manifested in the form of an elder—who joined his palms in reverent salutation and addressed Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, saying:
"O Great Being!..."

When the sentient beings of this Jambudvīpa pass away, if their small or large circles of relatives cultivate merit for them—by even offering vegetarian feasts and creating various roots of goodness—will that deceased person obtain great benefit and liberation?
Kṣitigarbha replied: "O Householder!
For the sake of all sentient beings of the future and the present, and by virtue of the Buddha’s majestic power, I have now briefly explained this matter."

O Elder, when all sentient beings of the future and the present approach the end of their lives, should they hear the name of even one Buddha, one Bodhisattva, or one Pratyekabuddha, regardless of whether they have committed transgressions or not, they shall all attain liberation.

"If there be men or women who, during their lifetime, failed to cultivate roots of goodness and committed many transgressions, after their death, if their relatives—both senior and junior—perform meritorious deeds and all manner of holy services on their behalf, they shall obtain but one-seventh of the benefit; the remaining six-sevenths of the merit will accrue as self-benefit to those who were alive."
For this reason, good men and women of the future and present should diligently cultivate themselves while they have the opportunity, so that each may obtain their own portion of merit.
The great ghost of impermanence arrives unexpectedly; when the spirit wanders into the darkness, one knows nothing of sin or blessing, remaining as if dull-witted and deaf for the seven weeks within.
Or, they may be in various offices, where their karmic fruits are debated and adjudicated; once determined, they receive rebirth according to their karma.
While this is not yet measured out, there are tens of millions of sorrows and sufferings—how much more so when one falls into the various evil destinies?

This deceased person, having not yet received rebirth, remains within the seven seven-day periods; in every thought-moment, they look toward their kinsmen and relatives to provide the power of merit to rescue and deliver them.
After this period has passed, one receives retribution according to one's karma; if one is a sinner, one will pass through thousands or hundreds of thousands of years without a day of liberation.
If one has committed the five crimes of immediate retribution, one will fall into the great hells and suffer all manner of miseries for thousands and tens of thousands of kalpas.
"Furthermore, householder!
When such sentient beings who have committed sinful karma reach the end of their lives, their kinsmen and relatives will perform memorial feasts to assist them on the path of karma."
Before the meal is finished, and during the course of preparing the meal, do not discard rice-wash water or vegetable leaves on the ground.
Furthermore, until all the food has been offered to the Buddha and the Sangha, one must not eat beforehand.
If one violates the rules regarding food or fails to be diligent, that person at the end of life will gain no benefit whatsoever.
However, if one is diligent in maintaining purity and makes offerings to the Buddha and the Sangha, that person at the end of life will obtain one-seventh of the merit.
Therefore, householder!

If the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa can, for the sake of their parents or even their kinsmen, perform a vegetarian feast offering after their deaths with a sincere and earnest mind, such people will benefit whether they are living or deceased.
When these words were spoken, there were thousands of millions of billions of *nayuta* of *yāma* spirits from the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven palace who all gave rise to the immeasurable mind of bodhi.
The Elder Mahāprajñā paid his respects and withdrew.

Chapter Eight: The Chapter on the Praise of the Multitude of King Yama. At that time, within the Cakravāḍa Mountains, there were immeasurable kings of ghosts who, together with the Devaputra Yama, went to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven and arrived at the place where the Buddha was.
These are the so-called King of Ghosts of Malicious Poison, the King of Many Evils, the King of Great Strife, the King of White Tigers,
the King of Blood Tigers, the King of Red Tigers, the King of Scattering Calamities, the King of Flying Bodies,
the King of Lightning Light, the King of Wolf Fangs, the King of a Thousand Eyes, and the Ghost that Devours Beasts.
The King, the Ghost-King Who Bears Stones, the Ghost-King Who Governs Waste, the Ghost-King Who Governs Calamity,

the Ghost-King Who Governs Food, the Ghost-King Who Governs Wealth, the Ghost-King Who Governs Livestock, the Ghost-King Who Governs Birds, the Ghost-King Who Governs Beasts, the Ghost-King Who Governs Demons,
the Ghost-King Who Governs Childbirth, the Ghost-King Who Governs Life, and the Ghost-King Who Governs Disease.
The King, the King of the Ghosts Who Master the Precipices, the Three-Eyed King of Ghosts,
