the King Kṛtya, the Great Kṛtya King, the King Anātha, and the Great Anātha King.
These great kings of ghosts, along with hundreds of thousands of minor ghost kings each, all reside within Jambudvīpa; each has their own domain and each has their own jurisdiction.

These kings of ghosts, together with the Son of Heaven Yama, receiving the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha and the strength of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, all proceeded to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven and stood to one side.
At that time, the Devaputra Yama knelt on his right knee with palms joined and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

We and all the kingly ghosts have now, by virtue of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power and the strength of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, been able to attend this great assembly in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven; it is because we have thereby obtained excellent benefit."
"I now have a minor doubt and venture to ask the World-Honored One; I only pray that the World-Honored One will compassionately explain it.
The Buddha told the Devaputra Yama:
"Ask whatever you wish, and I shall explain it for you."
At that time, the Devaputra Yama paid homage to the World-Honored One, turned his gaze toward Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

I observe that the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, within the six realms of existence, employs hundreds of thousands of skillful means to deliver sentient beings suffering from their karmic retributions, never declining out of weariness or fatigue.
This Great Bodhisattva possesses such inconceivable supernatural powers as these.
Yet, when sentient beings have escaped their retribution for sins, before long they fall again into the evil realms.
World-Honored One!
Since this Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha possesses such inconceivable spiritual power, why do sentient beings not rely upon the good paths to attain eternal liberation?
“I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain this for me.
The Buddha told the Devaputra Yama:
“The sentient beings of Jambudvīpa in the south are of a stubborn and fierce nature; they are difficult to harmonize and difficult to subdue.”
This great bodhisattva, throughout hundreds of thousands of kalpas, repeatedly rescues such sentient beings from head to toe, swiftly bringing them to liberation.
As for those people with karmic retribution for their sins, they may even fall into the great evil realms.
By the power of skillful means, the Bodhisattva extracts the fundamental karmic conditions and causes them to awaken to the events of their past lives.
From this point on, the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa, whose heavy habitual tendencies of evil have been bound, emerge and re-enter [the cycle] in rapid succession.
Bodhisattva Laushe has undergone many kalpas and brings about deliverance.
It is like a person who, having lost his way home, mistakenly enters a perilous path.
Within that perilous path, there are many yakṣas, as well as tigers, wolves, lions, vipers, snakes, and scorpions.
Thus, those deluded people, while in the midst of this dangerous road, will encounter various poisons in the space of a mere moment.
There was a friend who was highly proficient in great arts and skilled in suppressing poisons, including those of yakṣas and other malevolent toxins.
He encountered a person lost on the way who intended to enter a perilous path, and spoke to him, saying: "Alas!..."
"O man! For what purpose have you entered this path?
What extraordinary art do you possess that can subdue all poisons?"
Upon suddenly hearing these words, the lost traveler finally realized the perilous nature of the path; he immediately retreated, seeking to escape this way.

The spiritual friend took him by the hand and led him out of the dangerous road, sparing him from all evils and poisons, bringing him to a good path and granting him peace and happiness, and spoke to him, saying: "Alas!..."
Deluded one! From this day forward, do not tread upon this path.
Those who enter this road find it exceedingly difficult to escape, and they further lose their lives.
This lost traveler also felt a profound sense of gratitude.
As they were about to part, their acquaintance spoke again:
"If you encounter relatives, acquaintances, or other travelers—whether men or women—tell them that this road is fraught with many poisons and evils, where lives are lost."
"Do not allow this assembly to bring about their own deaths.

For this reason, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, endowed with great compassion, rescues sentient beings suffering from the retribution of their sins, causing them to be reborn among devas and humans so that they may experience sublime bliss.
These multitudes of offenders, having realized the suffering of the paths of karma, shall attain liberation and escape, never again to undergo such experience.
They are like a lost person who has mistakenly entered a perilous path; upon encountering a spiritual friend who guides them out, they shall never enter it again.
Upon encountering others, he further exhorts them not to enter, saying:
"Because of this delusion, I have attained liberation; having reached the end, I shall never enter again.

Yet if they were to step back in once more, they would still be led astray by delusion, failing to realize the perilous path where they previously fell, and might even lose their lives as if falling into an evil realm.
By the power of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva’s skillful means, they are enabled to attain liberation and be reborn among humans or devas;
yet they soon enter [the hells] once more. If their karmic fetters are heavy, they will dwell forever in hell with no time of liberation.
At that time, the King of Malevolent Poison Ghosts joined his palms in reverence and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
We ghost kings are immeasurable in number; within Jambudvīpa, some benefit people while others harm them, each being different."
However, due to this karmic retribution, my retinue wanders throughout the world, where evil prevails and goodness is scarce.
We pass by the households of men, whether they be cities, towns, villages, or private estates and dwellings.

There may be men or women who cultivate virtuous deeds as small as a single hair, even hanging up a single banner or canopy, offering a little incense or a few flowers to the images of the Buddha and the Bodhisattvas, or reciting the honored sutras, burning incense to offer to a single line or a single verse.
"We, the kings of ghosts, pay homage to this person as we do to the Buddhas of the past, present, and future.
We command all the minor ghosts—each possessing great power—as well as those belonging to the local lands, to provide protection."
May no evil matters, untimely calamities, malignant diseases, or sudden afflictions—nor even any disagreeable events—approach this house or its vicinity, let alone enter its doors.
The Buddha praised the King of Ghosts: “Excellent! Excellent!”
Since you and Yama are able to protect these sons and daughters of good family in this manner, I shall also inform Brahmā and Śakra, commanding them to guard and protect you.
When these words were spoken, there was a king of ghosts in the assembly named Zhujing (Lord of Life), who addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
By the karmic conditions of my original vocation, I preside over the lives of those in Jambudvīpa; whether they are born or die, I am the one who governs them all.”
In my original vow, I most deeply desire to bring benefit.
Yet these sentient beings do not understand my intention, which causes both themselves and me to find no peace within the cycle of birth and death.
"Why is this? When people of Jambudvīpa are first born—whether male or female—at the very moment of birth, they perform only virtuous deeds, which increase the prosperity of their homes."
This shall cause the land itself to be immeasurably joyful, protecting both mother and child so they attain great peace and happiness, and bringing benefit to their kin.
Once the child has been born, take care not to kill or harm it; instead, provide the birthing mother with various fresh and delicious foods.
Furthermore, by gathering a vast retinue, drinking wine, eating meat, and indulging in songs and music played on strings and pipes, one causes both mother and child to find no peace or happiness.
"Why is this so? [he asked.]
At the time of this difficult childbirth, there are countless malevolent spirits, as well as *wangliang* and spectral demons, who desire to consume the raw flesh and blood.
I have already commanded the local deities and the spirits of the dwelling place to protect the mother and child, ensuring they remain peaceful and secure, and that they obtain benefit.
When such a person perceives this as peace and security, they immediately prepare offerings of merit to repay the local deities;

yet instead, these acts turn into causes for slaughter. Gathering their kinsmen together, they consequently incur calamity and receive its retribution themselves, causing both mother and child to suffer ruin.

"Furthermore, regarding those in Jambudvīpa who are approaching the end of their lives—regardless of whether they have been virtuous or evil—I desire that these dying persons shall not fall into the evil realms, let alone those who have themselves cultivated roots of goodness, for this increases my power."

When those people in Jambudvīpa who have practiced good deeds approach the end of their lives, there are likewise hundreds of thousands of spirits from the evil realms who may transform themselves into parents or even various kinsmen to lead the deceased away and cause them to fall into the evil realms; how much more so for those who have originally committed evil?
“World-Honored One!

When men and women of Jambudvīpa approach the end of their lives, their consciousness becomes clouded and obscured; they cannot distinguish between good and evil, and even their eyes and ears no longer perceive or hear anything.”
For these kinsmen and attendants, one must provide great offerings, recite and chant the honored sutras, and invoke the names of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Through such virtuous conditions, they can cause the deceased to leave behind all evil realms, and cause all demons, ghosts, and spirits to retreat and disperse.
World-Honored One!

When all sentient beings approach the end of their lives, if they are able to hear the name of a single Buddha, the name of a single Bodhisattva, or even a single phrase or verse from a Mahāyāna sūtra, I observe that such persons—except for the crime of committing one of the five heinous acts of immediate retribution—will immediately be liberated from all minor evil karma that would otherwise cause them to fall into the evil realms.
The Buddha said to the King of Ghosts who Commands Life:
"Because of your great compassion, you are able to make such a great vow to protect all sentient beings within the cycle of birth and death."

If, in future ages, there should be men or women who, upon reaching the time of their birth and death, you must not retreat from this vow, but ensure they are all liberated and forever attain peace and happiness.
The King of Ghosts addressed the Buddha, saying:

“Please do not have such concerns; until this form of mine comes to an end, I shall protect the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa in every thought-moment, so that they may attain peace and happiness both at birth and at death.”
"I only wish that all sentient beings, at the time of birth and death, would believe and accept my words; then there would be none who do not attain liberation and obtain great benefit.
At that time, the Buddha told Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva:

"This Great King of Ghosts, the Lord of Life, has already passed through hundreds of thousands of lifetimes as a great king of ghosts, protecting sentient beings throughout the cycle of birth and death."
This is a Great Being who, out of compassion and aspiration, manifests in the form of a great ghost, though he is not actually a ghost.
After the passing of one hundred and seventy kalpas, he shall attain Buddhahood and be named the Tathāgata Formless (Animitta).
The kalpa is named Peaceful Bliss, and the world is named Pure Abode.
The lifespan of that Buddha is incalculable kalpas,
O Kṣitigarbha!
This great King of Ghosts is such that his deeds are inconceivable; the heavenly beings and humans he delivers are likewise beyond measure.
Chapter Nine: Invoking the Buddha’s Name At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I now expound upon matters of benefit for the sake of future sentient beings, so that they may attain great benefit within the cycle of birth and death.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant me leave to speak.
The Buddha addressed Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva:

"Now that you wish to give rise to compassion and rescue all sentient beings of the six realms from their karmic suffering and pain, and to expound these inconceivable matters, this is precisely the right time; you should speak of them immediately."
"I shall enter nirvana so that you may fulfill this vow early; thus, I too shall have no anxiety regarding all sentient beings in the present and the future.
Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
In the past, immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Anantatanu Tathāgata.
If any man or woman hears this Buddha’s name and gives rise to even a moment of reverent respect, they shall immediately transcend the grave sins of birth and death for forty kalpas.
How much more so for those who mold images, paint icons, make offerings, and offer praise?
Such a person shall obtain merit that is immeasurable and boundless.
Furthermore, in the past, during kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Ratnagarbha Tathāgata.

If there are men or women who, upon hearing these buddha-names, give rise to the mind of refuge for even the duration of a finger-snap, such persons shall never again regress from the unsurpassed path.
Furthermore, in the past, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Padmottara Tathāgata.

If any man or woman hears this Buddha’s name pass through their faculty of hearing, that person shall be reborn among the gods of the six desire heavens a thousand times; how much more so if they recite it with a sincere heart?
"Furthermore, in the past, incalculable, unspeakably many *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Siṃhanāda Tathāgata.

If any man or woman hears this Buddha’s name and takes refuge in him for a single thought-moment, that person shall encounter immeasurable Buddhas, who will touch their heads and bestow upon them a prophecy of enlightenment."
Furthermore, in the past, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Krakucchanda Buddha.

If there are men or women who, upon hearing this Buddha’s name, pay homage with a sincere mind or offer praise, these people shall become Great Brahma Kings within the assemblies of the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa and receive a prediction of their future enlightenment.
"Furthermore, in the past, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Vipaśyin.
If any man or woman hears this Buddha’s name, they will never again fall into the evil realms, but shall always be reborn among humans or devas, experiencing supreme and wondrous bliss."
"Furthermore, in the past, during immeasurable and incalculable kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Ratnashrī Tathāgata.
If any man or woman hears this Buddha’s name, they will ultimately never fall into the evil realms, but will always dwell in the heavens, receiving supreme and wondrous bliss."
"Furthermore, in the past, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Ratnākara Tathāgata.
If any man or woman, upon hearing this Buddha’s name, gives rise to a mind of reverence, that person will before long attain the fruit of Arhatship."
"Furthermore, in the past, immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas ago, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world named Kāṣāyadhvaja Tathāgata.
If any man or woman hears this Buddha’s name, they shall transcend the sins of birth and death for one hundred great kalpas."
"Furthermore, in the past, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world, named Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū Tathāgata.

If any man or woman hears this Buddha’s name, that person shall encounter Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, who will extensively preach the Dharma for them, and they will surely attain Bodhi."

Furthermore, in the past, there were Buddhas such as Pure Moon Buddha, Mountain King Buddha, Supreme Wisdom Buddha, Pure Name King Buddha, Accomplished Wisdom Buddha, Unsurpassed Buddha, Wondrous Sound Buddha, Full Moon Buddha, and Moon-Faced Buddha; indeed, there were unspeakably many such Buddhas.
“World-Honored One!

All sentient beings of the present and future—whether gods or humans, whether men or women—who merely succeed in recollecting the name of a single Buddha will gain immeasurable merit; how much more so for those who recollect many names?”
These sentient beings, at the time of birth and at the time of death, will naturally attain great benefit and shall never fall into the evil realms.

If there is a person whose life is nearing its end, and even a single member of their family or kin recites the name of a single Buddha aloud for the sake of that sick person, that dying person—excepting the five crimes of immediate retribution—will have all other karmic retributions completely extinguished.

Although these five offenses of immediate retribution are extremely grave, such that one may not find escape for billions of kalpas, if at the time of death another person recites the Buddha’s name for them, even within those sins they will gradually be extinguished.
"How much more so for sentient beings who, by their own declaration and reflection, shall obtain immeasurable merit and extinguish immeasurable sins.

Chapter Ten: The Chapter on Comparing the Merit of Giving. At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, rose from his seat, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
I observe the sentient beings within the paths of karma and weigh their acts of giving; there are those whose merit is light and those whose is heavy:
some receive blessings for one lifetime, some for ten lifetimes, and some who receive great benefit and merit for a hundred or a thousand lifetimes.
"What is the meaning of this?
I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain it for me.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva:
"I am now, in this assembly of all beings within the palace of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, speaking of the giving practiced in Jambudvīpa and weighing the relative gravity of its merits.
You should listen attentively; I shall speak for you."
Kṣitigarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“I have doubts regarding this matter; I wish and desire to hear [the explanation].
The Buddha told Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva:

“In Jambudvīpa, there are kings, ministers, great elders, great kṣatriyas, great brāhmaṇas, and others, who may encounter those who are most wretched and impoverished, even down to those who are crippled, mute, deaf, mentally deficient, or blind—those of various such incomplete faculties.”

When these great kings and others wish to practice giving, if they can possess great compassion, lower their minds with a smile, and personally distribute gifts everywhere—or have others give them—while consoling the recipients with gentle words.

The merit and benefit obtained by these kings and others is equal to the benefit of the merit from making offerings to as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in a hundred Ganges Rivers. Why is this?

Because these kings and others have given rise to a heart of great compassion toward those who are most poor and lowly, as well as those who are incomplete; therefore, their merit and benefit result in such a reward.
Throughout hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, they shall always possess the seven treasures in abundance, let alone the enjoyment of food and clothing.
"Furthermore, Kṣitigarbha!

If in future ages there are kings, or even Brahmins and others, who encounter a Buddha’s stupa or temple, or even an image of a Buddha, or images of Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, or Pratyekabuddhas, and personally provide for them with offerings and almsgiving."
These kings and others shall attain the body of Śakra for three kalpas and experience supreme, wondrous bliss.
If they can dedicate the merit of this giving to the Dharma-realm, these great kings and others will constantly serve as Great Brahmā Kings for ten kalpas.
"Furthermore, Kṣitigarbha!

If in future ages there should be kings, or even Brahmins and others, who encounter the stūpas and temples of former Buddhas, or come upon scriptures and images that have become ruined, dilapidated, or fallen into decay, and are able to give rise to the resolve to repair them."
These kings and others, whether arranging the offerings themselves or encouraging others, even those numbering in the hundreds or thousands, establish karmic connections through such giving.
Throughout hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, these kings shall always take birth as universal monarchs (cakravartin).
Likewise, those others who likewise practiced giving shall, throughout hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, always take birth as the bodies of minor kings.

Furthermore, if they can give rise to the mind of dedication before a stupa or temple, then these kings and all such people will ultimately attain the Buddha-way; by virtue of this karmic fruit, it shall be immeasurable and boundless.
"Furthermore, Kṣitigarbha!

In future ages, there may be kings, as well as brahmins and others, who, upon seeing the elderly and the infirm, or women in childbirth, should for even a single moment conceive a heart of great compassion, providing them with medicine, food and drink, and bedding to bring them peace and happiness."
Such merit and benefit are most inconceivable:
for one hundred kalpas, one shall constantly be the Lord of the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven;
for two hundred kalpas, one shall constantly be the Lord of the Six Desire Heavens.
They will ultimately attain Buddhahood and never again fall into the evil realms; even throughout hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, their ears shall not hear the sound of suffering.
"Furthermore, Kṣitigarbha!

If, in future ages, there are kings, brahmins, and others who are able to perform such acts of giving, they will obtain immeasurable merit; if they further dedicate this merit, regardless of its magnitude, they will ultimately attain Buddhahood—how much more so the rewards of Śakra, Brahmā, or a universal monarch!
Therefore, Kṣitigarbha!
You should universally exhort all sentient beings to train themselves in this way.
Furthermore, Kṣitigarbha!

In future ages, if good sons or good daughters plant even a small root of goodness within the Buddha-dharma—be it as slight as a hair, a speck of dust, or a grain of sand—the benefit and merit they receive shall be beyond all comparison.
Furthermore, Kṣitigarbha!

In future ages, if there are good men or good women who encounter images of Buddhas, images of Bodhisattvas, images of Pratyekabuddhas, or images of Wheel-Turning Kings, and offer them gifts and worship, they shall obtain immeasurable merit; they will constantly dwell among devas and humans, experiencing supreme and wondrous bliss.
If one can dedicate [the merit] to the Dharma-realm, the blessings and benefits for such a person are beyond comparison.
"Furthermore, Kṣitigarbha!

In future ages, if there are good men or good women who encounter Mahāyāna sūtras, or hear even a single verse or a single phrase, and give rise to a heart of profound sincerity, praising and revering them, and making offerings through giving."
Such a person shall obtain a great fruit of retribution, immeasurable and boundless.
If they can dedicate this toward the Dharma-realm, its merit is beyond comparison.
"Furthermore, Kṣitigarbha!

If, in future ages, there are good men or good women who encounter new Buddha-stūpas, temples, or Mahāyāna sūtras, and offer them gifts and sustenance, gaze upon them with reverence, praise them, and pay homage with palms joined;
or if they encounter old or dilapidated ones, they repair and maintain them—whether acting alone out of their own resolve or exhorting many others to join them in this resolve.
Throughout thirty such lifetimes, these individuals will constantly serve as minor kings,
while their patrons will constantly serve as universal monarchs (cakravartin), using virtuous teachings to convert and transform those minor kings.
"Furthermore, Kṣitigarbha!

In future ages, if there are good men or good women who, within the Buddha-dharma, plant roots of goodness—whether by practicing giving and making offerings, repairing stupas and temples, or binding and arranging the scriptures—even if it be as little as a single hair, a single speck of dust, a single grain of sand, or a single drop of water.
If such virtuous deeds are dedicated solely to the Dharma-realm, the merit of that person will cause them to experience supreme and wondrous bliss for hundreds of thousands of lifetimes.

However, if they dedicate them only to their own family and kin, or for their own personal benefit, the resulting fruit will lead to the enjoyment of happiness for only three lifetimes—giving up ten thousand rewards for the sake of one.
"Therefore, Kṣitigarbha! Such are the matters regarding the causes and conditions of giving.
Chapter Eleven: The Earth Deity Protects the Dharma At that time, the Earth Deity Vajraśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Since ancient times, I have gazed upon and paid homage to immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, all of whom possess inconceivable supernormal powers and wisdom, extensively delivering sentient beings.”
This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha has made profound and weighty vows among all bodhisattvas.
World-Honored One!
This Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha possesses great karmic affinity with Jambudvīpa.

Even Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteśvara, and Maitreya transform themselves into hundreds of thousands of physical forms to deliver beings throughout the six realms; yet their vows still have an ultimate limit.
This Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha has made vows for kalpas as numerous as the sands of a thousand billion Ganges Rivers to teach and transform all sentient beings throughout the six realms of existence.
“World-Honored One!

I observe that among future and present sentient beings, in their places of residence, they will construct small shrines out of earth, stone, bamboo, or wood upon clean ground in the southern direction.
In this regard, if one is able to mold or paint, or even fashion images of Kṣitigarbha from gold, silver, copper, or iron, and then burn incense to make offerings,
gaze upon them with reverence, and offer praise— wherever such a person dwells, they shall immediately obtain ten kinds of benefits.
What are the ten? First, the land shall be fertile and rich.
Second, one's household shall enjoy perpetual peace and security.
Third, those who have previously passed away will be reborn in the heavens.
Fourth, those currently living will have their lifespans increased.
Fifth, whatever they seek shall be fulfilled according to their wishes.
Sixth, there shall be no disasters of water or fire.
Seventh, all depletion and waste shall be dispelled.
Eighth, evil dreams shall be utterly cut off.
Ninth, they will be protected by divine guardians as they come and go.
Tenth, they will frequently encounter the causes for attaining sagehood.
"World-Honored One!..."
In future ages, as well as for sentient beings in the present, if they can perform such offerings in the direction where [the image] resides, they shall obtain such benefits.
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

In future ages, if there are good men or good women who, in their place of residence, possess this sutra as well as an image of a bodhisattva, and these people are further able to recite and read the sutra and make offerings to the bodhisattva.”

Day and night, I shall constantly use my original spiritual power to protect this person; even against water, fire, thieves, robbers, great calamities, or minor misfortunes—all such evil matters shall be entirely extinguished.
The Buddha told the Earth Deity Dṛḍhā:
"Your great supernatural power is such that few deities can approach it. Why is this?"
The land of Jambudvīpa is entirely protected by you.
Even down to the grasses, trees, sand, and stones, the rice, hemp, bamboo, reeds, grains, and precious treasures that arise from the earth—all exist because of your power.

Furthermore, you shall constantly extol the deeds of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva that benefit sentient beings; your merit and spiritual powers shall be hundreds of thousands of times greater than those of ordinary earth deities.

If, in future ages, there are good men or good women who make offerings to Bodhisattvas and recite this sutra, practicing even according to a single matter from the *Kṣitigarbha-pūrvapraṇidhāna-sūtra*, you shall, by means of your original spiritual power, protect and sustain them.
Do not allow any calamities or unfavorable matters to ever reach their ears, much less let them suffer them.
It is not only because you alone protect these people; Śakra and Brahmā, along with their retinues and the hosts of devas, shall also protect them.
For what reason do they receive such protection from the noble sages?
It is entirely because they have gazed upon and paid homage to the image of Kṣitigarbha, and because they have recited this Sūtra of the Original Vow.
Consequently, they will naturally and ultimately transcend the ocean of suffering and realize the bliss of nirvāṇa.
For this reason, one shall obtain great protection.

Chapter Twelve: Benefits of Seeing and Hearing At that time, from the crown of his head, the World-Honored One emitted hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of rays of light from his great *ūrṇā* mark—namely:
The light of the white ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the great white ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the auspicious ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the great auspicious ūrṇā-kośa mark,
the light of the jade ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the great jade ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the purple ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the great purple ūrṇā-kośa mark,
the light of the blue ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the great blue ūrṇā-kośa mark, and the light of the emerald ūrṇā-kośa mark.
The light of the great blue ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the red ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the great red ūrṇā-kośa mark,
the light of the green ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the great green ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the golden ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the great golden ūrṇā-kośa mark,

the light of the auspicious cloud ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the great auspicious cloud ūrṇā-kośa mark, the light of the thousand-spoked wheel ūrṇā-kośa, and the light of the great thousand-spoked wheel ūrṇā-kośa.
The light from the hair-tuft, the jewel-wheel hair-tuft light, the great jewel-wheel hair-tuft light,
the sun-wheel hair-tuft light, the great sun-wheel hair-tuft light, the moon-wheel hair-tuft light, the great moon-wheel hair-tuft light,
the palace hair-tuft light, the great palace hair-tuft light, the ocean-cloud hair-tuft light, and the great ocean-cloud hair-tuft light.

Having emitted such rays of light from the *ūrṇā* between his eyebrows, he issued a subtle and wondrous sound, addressing the great assembly, the eight classes of beings including devas and nāgas, humans, and non-humans:

"Listen as I today, in the palace of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, extol and praise the deeds of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva—his works that benefit humans and devas, his inconceivable deeds, his deeds that transcend the causes of the holy ones, his realization of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*), and his ultimate non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."

When these words were spoken, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the assembly named Avalokiteśvara, who rose from his seat, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha possesses great compassion; out of pity for sentient beings suffering from their transgressions, he manifests thousands of millions of billions of bodies throughout thousands of millions of billions of worlds.

Regarding all these merits and inconceivable powers of majestic spiritual authority, I have heard that the World-Honored One, together with the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions, with one voice and in unison, praised the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, saying:
"Even if all the Buddhas of the past, present, and future were to speak of his merits, they could not exhaustively describe them."
Just now, we were further graced by the World-Honored One’s proclamation to the great assembly regarding the desire to extol the benefits and other matters concerning Kṣitigarbha.

We only pray that the World-Honored One will, for the sake of all sentient beings of the present and future, extol the inconceivable deeds of Kṣitigarbha, so that the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas, may gaze upon him with reverence and obtain merit.
The Buddha told Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva:
"In this Sahā world, you have great karmic affinities.

Whether they be devas or nāgas, men or women, spirits or ghosts—even down to sentient beings of the six realms suffering from their transgressions—those who hear your name, see your form, yearn for you, or praise you, these sentient beings shall certainly never regress from the Unsurpassed Way. They will constantly be reborn among humans and devas, fully experiencing wondrous bliss; when their causes and effects ripen, they will encounter a Buddha and receive a prediction of enlightenment."

You now possess great compassion and pity for sentient beings, as well as for the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas; therefore, listen as I proclaim the inconceivable benefits of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.
"You should listen attentively; I shall now speak of it.
Avalokiteśvara said, "So be it, World-Honored One!"
“I wish to hear it with joy.
The Buddha told Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva:

“In the worlds of the future and the present, there are devas and humans whose celestial blessings have been exhausted, and for whom the five signs of decline appear; some even fall into the evil realms.”

When such signs appear for these devas and humans—whether male or female—if they see the image of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, or hear the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, and gaze upon him or prostrate themselves even once, the merit of these devas and humans will increase further, they shall experience great happiness, and they will never again fall into the retribution of the three evil realms.

How much more so for those who see or hear of Bodhisattvas and offer them gifts and worship with various incenses, flowers, robes, food and drink, precious gems, and necklaces—the merit, blessings, and benefits obtained will be immeasurable and boundless.
"Furthermore, Avalokiteśvara!

If, in all worlds of the future and present, sentient beings of the six realms of existence, at the time of their death, should hear the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, and that single sound passes through their faculty of hearing, these sentient beings shall never again experience the suffering of the three evil paths."
How much more so when, at the time of death, the parents and kinsmen fashion an image of Kṣitigarbha out of clay or paint using the house, wealth, treasures, and clothing of the dying person.

Or, while the patient has not yet passed away, they may see or hear with their own eyes and ears that their kinsmen and relatives are using the family home, treasures, and other assets for their own sake to fashion or paint an image of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.
If such a person is fated by karmic retribution to suffer from a grave illness, by virtue of this merit, they shall immediately recover and their lifespan shall be increased.

If such a person’s life is destined to end by karmic retribution, and should they possess various obstacles of sin and karma such that they ought to fall into the evil realms, by virtue of this merit, after their death they shall be reborn among humans or devas, experiencing supreme and wondrous bliss, and all their sinful obstacles shall be completely extinguished.
"Furthermore, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva!
If in future ages there are men or women who, at the time of nursing, or at three years, five years, or ten years of age and below, lose their parents, or even lose their brothers and sisters."
As this person grew older, he began to long for his parents and his kinsmen, wondering in which realm they had fallen,
in which world they were born,
or in which heaven they resided.

If such a person can mold or paint an image of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, or even merely hear his name, looking upon it once or prostrating once for one day up to seven days without abandoning their initial resolve—whether hearing the name, seeing the form, gazing upon it, prostrating, or making offerings.

If the kinsmen and attendants of such a person, due to the causes and conditions of their karma, should fall into the evil realms, they shall, by calculating the number of kalpas [they would have spent there], immediately attain liberation and be reborn among humans or devas by virtue of having fashioned images of Kṣitigarbha—whether through clay, painting, or carving—and having gazed upon and paid homage to them.
Those who experience superior and wondrous bliss shall, by virtue of this merit, further increase their noble causes and enjoy immeasurable happiness.
If this person can further, for seven times seven days, single-mindedly gaze upon and worship an image of Kṣitigarbha and recite his name ten thousand times,
they shall cause the Bodhisattva to manifest his boundless body and fully inform them regarding the realms where their kinsmen have been reborn;
or, within a dream, the Bodhisattva will manifest great supernatural power and personally lead this person through various worlds to see their kinsmen.

Furthermore, if one can recite the name of this Bodhisattva a thousand times every day for a period of one thousand days, that person shall receive the protection of the spirits of the local land dispatched by the Bodhisattva for their entire life.

In this present world, their food and clothing will be abundant, they will be free from all illness and suffering, and even calamitous events will not enter their door, let alone afflict their person.
Such a person will ultimately receive the Bodhisattva’s empowerment upon the crown of their head and their formal prediction of enlightenment. Furthermore, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva!

If, in future ages, there are good men or good women who wish to give rise to a vast and great heart of compassion to rescue and deliver all sentient beings; who wish to cultivate unexcelled bodhi; or who wish to transcend the triple world.

If these people see the image of Kṣitigarbha or hear his name, they take refuge in him with a sincere heart, making offerings and paying homage to him with incense, flowers, clothing, precious gems, and food and drink.
"The aspirations of these good men and women shall be swiftly fulfilled, forever free from obstacles.
Furthermore, Avalokiteśvara!

If in future ages there are good men and good women who wish to seek hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of vows and hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of matters pertaining to the present and the future, they need only take refuge in, gaze upon, prostrate before, make offerings to, and praise the image of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha; then all such vows and requests shall be fully accomplished."

Furthermore, I pray that Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, endowed with great compassion, will forever protect me; may this person, within their dreams, receive the Bodhisattva’s empowerment upon the crown of the head and his prophetic assurance.
"Furthermore, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva!
If, in future ages, there are good men or good women who conceive a deep sense of preciousness for the Mahāyāna sūtras and, giving rise to an inconceivable mind, desire to read and recite them."
Even if they encounter an enlightened teacher who instructs them until they are proficient, they forget what they have just learned; as months and years pass, they are unable to recite it.
These good sons and others possess karmic obstructions from past lives that have not yet been eliminated; therefore, they lack the disposition for reading and reciting the Mahāyāna sūtras.

If such a person hears the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva or beholds an image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, they shall fully express their sincere heart with reverence and further make offerings to the Bodhisattva with incense, flowers, clothing, food and drink, and all manner of playthings.

Place one cup of pure water before the Bodhisattva and let it remain there for one day and one night; thereafter, with palms joined, request that he partake of it, turning your head toward the south and maintaining a mind of utmost sincerity and gravity as you bring it to your mouth.

Once the practice of taking water has been completed, one must carefully avoid the five pungent vegetables, alcohol, meat, sexual misconduct, false speech, and all forms of killing for either seven days or twenty-one days.

These sons and daughters of good family, within their dreams, will fully behold the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha manifesting his boundless body, who shall bestow upon them the water of empowerment at that very spot.

Upon awakening from that dream, that person immediately attains clarity of mind; whatever corresponds to these scriptures passes through their faculty of hearing only once, and they shall remember it forever, never forgetting even a single word or a single verse.
"Furthermore, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva!
If in future ages there are people who lack sufficient clothing and food,
and whose prayers for what they seek go unfulfilled;
Either they will suffer from many illnesses, or experience much misfortune and decline;
their homes will be unstable, and their kin and retinues will be scattered;
or various calamitous events will frequently come to afflict them.
During their sleep and dreams, they will experience much alarm and fear.
If such persons as these hear the name of Kṣitigarbha, see the form of Kṣitigarbha, and with a sincere heart pay him reverence, reciting his name ten thousand times, [they shall be delivered].

These various unpleasant matters will gradually vanish, and one will immediately attain peace and happiness; food and clothing will be abundant, and even in dreams, everything will be peaceful and joyful.
"Furthermore, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva!

If in future ages there are good men or good women who, whether for the sake of making a living, for public or private affairs, for the sake of life and death, or due to urgent business, enter mountain forests, cross rivers and seas, or encounter great waters, or travel along perilous paths."

This person should first recite the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva ten thousand times; wherever they travel, spirits and deities will provide protection, and whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, they shall forever abide in peace and happiness.
"Even if they encounter tigers, wolves, lions, or any other poisonous and harmful creatures, none shall be able to harm them.
The Buddha told Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva:
"This Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva has a great karmic affinity with Jambudvīpa."
If one were to speak of the benefits derived from seeing or hearing [the name of] sentient beings, even in hundreds of thousands of kalpas, one could not exhaustively describe them.
Therefore, Avalokiteśvara!
"By your supernatural power, propagate this sutra so that the sentient beings of the Sahā world may enjoy peace and happiness for hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"I observe the majestic spiritual power of Kṣitigarbha; Even in kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, it would be difficult to exhaustively describe it."
To see, hear, behold, or pay homage for even a single thought-moment brings immeasurable benefit to humans and devas.
Whether male or female, or even among dragons and spirits, those whose retribution is exhausted and who would otherwise fall into evil realms—
by taking refuge with a sincere heart in the body of this Great Being, their lifespan shall increase and their karmic obstacles be eliminated.
Those who lost their parents' affection at a young age, do not know where their spirits and souls now abide;
brothers, sisters, and all their kin, whom they have known since birth, are all now unrecognized.
Whether sculpted or painted, one should gaze upon and worship the body of the Great Being with compassionate longing, never for a moment letting it go;
by reciting His name throughout twenty-one days,
the Bodhisattva shall manifest His boundless form and reveal the realm where His retinue is reborn, so that even those who have fallen into the evil destinies may swiftly find liberation.
If one can remain不退 (non-retrogressive) in this initial resolve, One shall immediately receive the holy prediction with a touch of the crown.
Those who wish to cultivate unsurpassed bodhi, And even seek liberation from the suffering of the three realms—
Such persons, having already given rise to the mind of great compassion, Should first gaze upon and pay homage to the image of the Great Being.
May all vows be swiftly fulfilled, And may no karmic obstacles ever hinder them.
Should there be one who resolves to recite this scripture, Desiring to deliver the deluded masses to the other shore—
Though they establish such inconceivable aspirations, They may forget it as soon as they read it, losing much that was gained.
Because such a person has karmic obstructions and delusions, they are unable to master the Mahāyāna sūtras.
By making offerings to Kṣitigarbha with incense, flowers, clothing, food, drink, and various playthings,
and by placing pure water before the Great Being, one should seek to consume it for one day and one night.
Arouse a heart of profound sincerity and be careful regarding the five pungent roots; refrain from alcohol, meat, sexual misconduct, and false speech.
For twenty-one days, do not commit acts of killing, but with a sincere mind, recollect the name of the Great Being.
Within the dream, one sees the boundless; upon awakening, one immediately gains sharp faculties of hearing.
It must be that the teachings of the sutras have passed through one's ears, never to be forgotten throughout ten million lifetimes.
Because this Great Being is inconceivable, he is able to cause these people to obtain such wisdom.
For sentient beings who are impoverished or afflicted by disease, whose households face misfortune and decline,
whose kin are separated from them, who find no peace even within their dreams, and whose seekers meet with failure and lack fulfillment— [he brings them relief].
If one reverently gazes upon and pays homage to the image of Kṣitigarbha with a sincere heart, all evil deeds will be extinguished;
even in dreams, one shall find complete peace, while clothing and food become abundant and one is protected by gods and spirits.
Whether entering mountain forests or crossing the sea, Facing venomous beasts and wicked men,
Evil deities, malevolent spirits, and fierce winds— May all such perils and every form of suffering be averted.
One should simply gaze upon and pay homage to, and make offerings to, the image of the Great Being Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva;
thus, within these mountains, forests, and great oceans, all evils shall be extinguished.

Avalokiteśvara, listen with a sincere heart to my words: The inexhaustible and inconceivable power of Kṣitigarbha could not be fully described even in hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas; thus I proclaim the great strength of this Bodhisattva.
If anyone hears the name of Kṣitigarbha, or even sees his image and pays him homage,
offering incense, flowers, robes, and food, they shall enjoy sublime bliss for hundreds of thousands of lifetimes.
If they can dedicate this merit to the Dharma-realm, they will ultimately attain Buddhahood and transcend birth and death.
"Therefore, Avalokiteśvara, you should know this and proclaim it throughout all lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.

Chapter Thirteen: Entrustment to Humans and Devas At that time, the World-Honored One raised his golden arm and again stroked the crown of the head of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, saying: "Kṣitigarbha!"
Kṣitigarbha!
Your supernatural powers are inconceivable; your compassion is inconceivable.
Your wisdom is inconceivable; your eloquence is inconceivable.
Even if all the Buddhas of the ten directions were to praise and proclaim these inconceivable matters of yours, they could not exhaust them within ten million kalpas.
"Kṣitigarbha! Kṣitigarbha!

Remember that today, amidst this great assembly of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, I once again entrust to you all those sentient beings among humans and devas who have not yet emerged from the triple world and remain within the burning house."

Do not let these sentient beings fall into the evil realms for even a single day and night, much less cause them to fall further into the five places of no interval or the Avīci Hell, where they would pass through thousands of millions of billions of kalpas without any prospect of release?

“Kṣitigarbha! The sentient beings of this Jambudvīpa are unstable in their dispositions; they mostly habituate themselves to evil. Even if they give rise to a virtuous mind, it recedes in an instant; if they encounter adverse conditions, [their evil] increases with every thought.”
For this reason, I shall divide this form into hundreds of thousands of billions of manifestations to deliver and liberate beings according to their respective faculties and natures.
Kṣitigarbha!
I now earnestly entrust you with the multitudes of devas and humans.

In future ages, if there are devas or humans, or sons and daughters of good family, who plant even a small root of goodness within the Buddha-dharma—be it as slight as a single hair, a speck of dust, a grain of sand, or a drop of water.
By the power of the Way, you shall protect these people, causing them to gradually cultivate the unsurpassed path and ensuring they do not fall back or lose their progress.
Furthermore, Kṣitigarbha!
In future ages, whether gods or humans, according to the retribution of their karma, may fall into the evil realms.

When they are on the verge of falling into the realms of rebirth, or have already reached the gates thereof, if these sentient beings can recollect the name of even one Buddha, the name of one Bodhisattva, or a single phrase or verse from a Mahāyāna sūtra.
For these sentient beings, you should use your supernatural powers and skillful means to rescue and deliver them.
To those people, manifest an infinite body to shatter the hells and dispatch them to be born in the heavens, where they may experience supreme and wondrous bliss.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
“The multitudes of devas and humans of the present and future, I now earnestly entrust to you.
By means of great supernormal powers and skillful expedients, Do not let them fall into the various evil realms.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I pray only that the World-Honored One will not be concerned.”

In future ages, if there are good men or good women who, within the Buddha-dharma, show even a single thought of reverence, I too shall, through hundreds of thousands of skillful means, deliver such persons and enable them to swiftly attain liberation from the cycle of birth and death.
"How much more so for those who hear of various virtuous deeds and practice them in every thought-moment?
They will naturally never regress from the unsurpassed path.
When these words were spoken, there was a bodhisattva in the assembly named Gaganagañja, who addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Having come from the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven myself, I have heard the Tathāgata praise the inconceivable majestic power and spiritual authority of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha.”

In future ages, if there are good men and good women, as well as all devas and nāgas, who hear this sutra and the name of Kṣitigarbha, or who behold and pay homage to his image, how many kinds of blessings and benefits shall they obtain?
“I only pray that the World-Honored One will briefly explain this for the sake of all beings of the future and the present.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha:
“Listen attentively!”
Listen attentively!
I shall explain this to you in detail.

If, in future ages, there are good men or good women who see an image of Kṣitigarbha, or hear this sutra, or even read and recite it; and who offer worship with incense, flowers, food and drink, clothing, and precious jewels; and who praise, gaze upon, and pay homage to him—they shall obtain twenty-eight kinds of benefits:
First, they are protected and remembered by devas and nāgas; second, their wholesome fruits increase daily;
third, they accumulate the supreme causes for sainthood; fourth, they do not regress from bodhi; fifth, their clothing and food are abundant; sixth, epidemics do not approach them;
seventh, they are free from the calamities of water and fire; eighth, they are without the misfortunes of thieves and bandits; ninth, people behold them with [reverence].
10. Reverence; 11. Deities and spirits provide assistance and support; 12. A woman transforms her female body into a male one;
13. Becoming a king’s consort or a minister’s wife; 14. Possessing the marks of physical excellence and beauty;
15. Rebirth many times in the heavens; 16. Or becoming a sovereign emperor; 17. Possessing innate wisdom and the power of life-reading (*jñāna* and *abhijñā*).
17. All requests are fulfilled; 18. one’s retinue is joyful; 19. all calamities are extinguished; 20.
the paths of karma are forever eliminated; 21. one has unhindered passage wherever one goes; 22.
one experiences peace and happiness in dreams at night; 23. deceased ancestors are freed from suffering; 24. [and so forth].
Twenty-fourth, they are born through the maturation of past merit; twenty-fifth, they are praised by all the sages;
twenty-sixth, they possess intelligence and sharp faculties; twenty-seventh, they abound in a heart of loving-kindness and compassion; twenty-eighth, they will ultimately attain Buddhahood.
"Furthermore, Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva!

If, in the present or the future, devas, nāgas, ghosts, or spirits hear the name of Kṣitigarbha, prostrate before the form of Kṣitigarbha, or hear of Kṣitigarbha’s original vows, deeds, and practices, and then praise and pay homage to him, they shall obtain seven kinds of benefits:

first, they will swiftly transcend to the stages of the sages; second, their evil karma will be extinguished; third, all Buddhas will protect and attend them; fourth, they will not regress from bodhi; fifth, their innate power will increase; sixth, they will attain full knowledge of their past lives; and seventh, they will ultimately achieve Buddhahood."

At that time, the unspeakably unspeakable number of all Tathāgatas who had come from the ten directions, along with the great Bodhisattvas and the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas, heard Śākyamuni Buddha extol and praise the inconceivable and great majestic spiritual power of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, and they marveled at this unprecedented occurrence.
At that time, the Trāyastriṃśa devas rained down immeasurable fragrant flowers, celestial robes, pearls, and necklaces, making offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha and Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.
The entire assembly, having together paid their respects once more, withdrew with palms joined.
*The Sutra on the Original Vows of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva*, Scroll II.
